task: Execute the interactive case-study plan through locally verified Phase 7 release tooling, then stop before protected release and Phase 8 human gates.
scoutSummary: Repository contracts, historical restoration evidence, frozen H5 output, publication policy, and the existing Pages workflow were inspected before implementation. Phases 1 through 6 supplied the bilingual Astro case study and playable H5 integration; Phase 7 now composes, audits, verifies, reviews, and smoke-tests an immutable local candidate.
acceptanceCriteria: Bilingual documentary routes, evidence joins, AI disclosures, and playable launch paths build as a static Astro site.
The audited raw Cocos output is copied byte-for-byte under /play/game/ without weakening the game-only audit.
The composed candidate is prefix-safe, deterministic, provenance-bound, and free of unapproved executable or media fetches.
The actual launcher performs no eager game request and preserves parent DOM, navigation, and storage while the embedded H5 loads, reloads, and is removed.

Release workflows keep untrusted site work off the Creator runner, pin actions and runtimes, bind human approval to immutable candidate identity, and preserve that identity across deploy-only retries.
Auto mode stops before live repository mutation, protected deployment, rollback, or human approval.
publicContracts: GitHub Pages base /pencil-blade-2026/ with the playable H5 at /pencil-blade-2026/play/game/.
Candidate approval request and post-deployment evidence are separate schema-valid nondeployable artifacts.
The release record binds commit, workflow run, candidate attempt, content digest, tree-manifest digest, site digest, and game digest.
A later deploy attempt may reuse the immutable candidate attempt but may not rebuild or silently change candidate identity.
Academic display permission and commercial release rights remain separate fail-closed dimensions.
blastRadius: Static site content, routes, assets, browser behavior, and accessibility.
Raw and nested H5 verification, runtime evidence, and shared-origin launcher behavior.
GitHub Actions trust boundaries, artifacts, protected Pages deployment, evidence collection, production smoke, and rollback procedure.
Publication, source, media, approval, and toolchain contracts.
